sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:39

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:39:1
items.html: Lo Mati in Keter, then it is Mati in Hochma, and the light of Hochma descends into her: For the coarseness of phase three of the Nukva of Keter returned and refined, and then the vessel of Keter turns her face downward and once more gives her remainder, that is, phase two, to Hochma, as before; and so the light of Hochma descended once again, as at first.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:39:2
items.html:
The seven sons that are in Bina are grown and do not need their mother, and then Bina rises to Hochma. The meaning is that after the light of Hochma descended to the vessel of Hochma, this illumination reaches the vessel of Bina as well, for the above reason that Aba and Ima emerge as one — that is, that they emerge on a single aspect of coarseness, and therefore they dwell as one, meaning that their level is equal, as above in the adjacent item, the passage beginning “and the light.” And since the illumination reached Bina, the light of Hesed, too, receives this illumination of Hochma, and then it attained its aspect of Gadlut [greatness], that is, the aspect of GAR of the VAK.
And this is what he says, “and then the seven sons that are in Bina are grown and do not need their mother.” For after they attained the illumination of Hochma they became grown, since they attained the aspect of a Rosh, and therefore they do not need their mother. For before this the VAK were the aspect of the light of Hassadim, without any illumination of Hochma, and therefore they had to receive their vitality from the vessel of Bina, which is the aspect of GAR and the aspect of essence; and they could not separate from the vessel of Bina to the vessels of the VAK, because of the lack of vitality, for there is no vitality and essence except from the aspect of Hochma. But now that they have attained the illumination of Hochma they have become grown, and they have standing and the power to expand into their own vessels.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:39:3
items.html:
And then Bina rises to Hochma. For it is impossible for the upper one to bestow to the lower one except through the turning of the face, that is, that it be in equivalence with the lower one, so that it is discerned as close to it and gives it its remainder. Therefore Bina rises to Hochma, that is, the male and the Nukva of Bina refine from their phase two to phase one, and phase one now becomes the face; and thereby the vessel of Bina is found face to face with the vessel of Hesed, for both of them are now of the coarseness of phase one, and this is what is called face to face. And then the male and female of the vessel of Bina depart and rise to the vessel of Hochma, and Hochma and Bina are found in a single vessel, of the aspect of Hochma; and now the rule of the vessel of Hochma is in the Partzuf.
And there is a further depth here. For in truth the aspect of Bina is still, from the root of the direct light, the aspect of the posterior toward Hochma, in the secret of the Yod [י] and the Nun [נ] of the Tzaddik, which are inverted one to the other, as is written in the Zohar, Bereshit, and as the ARI hinted here further on, in the secret of the words “for He delights in Hesed” — for Bina craves Hassadim more than Hochma. And therefore she had to rise to the vessel of Hochma, so that she should not stop the light of Hesed with her aspect of the posterior; and then the light of Hesed can receive a greater illumination from Hochma. And understand this.
